## Big Question {.role-slide}

What can an analysis claim when some linguistic measurements were never observed?

## Data {.role-slide}

A vowel study records duration, F1, and F3.

The F3 tracker fails for some tokens.

## Challenge {.role-slide}

A blank cell is not a measured value. Deleting or filling it can change the quantity being estimated.

## Possibility {.role-slide}

[**Imputation**](https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-historic.html) replaces a missing value with one or more estimates from a model or rule.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-historic.html
:::

## This Module {.role-slide .compact}

1. Represent where measurements are absent.
2. State how absence may depend on observed and unseen values.
3. Determine what deletion estimates.
4. Reconstruct missing cells and validate the procedure.

## Missingness patterns {.section-slide}

Representing blank cells

## Question {.role-slide}

Where are duration, F1, and F3 absent in the acoustic table?

## Answer {.role-slide}

A [**missingness indicator**](https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html) records whether a potential measurement was observed.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html
:::

## Method {.role-slide}

$$
R_{ij}=
\begin{cases}
1&\text{if }Y_{ij}\text{ is observed},\\
0&\text{if }Y_{ij}\text{ is missing}.
\end{cases}
$$

## Data {.role-slide .compact}

$$
\mathbf R=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1&1\\
1&1&0\\
1&1&1\\
1&0&0\\
1&1&1
\end{pmatrix}
$$

## Output {.role-slide}

Column counts locate measurements with loss.

Row counts locate tokens with little information.

Pattern counts locate measurements that disappear together.

## Challenge {.role-slide}

An association between vowel and missing F3 does not identify the process that caused the association.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

The missingness pattern is observed. Its generating mechanism is not.

## Missingness mechanisms {.section-slide}

Dependence on observed and unseen measurements

## Answer {.role-slide}

A [**missingness mechanism**](https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html) states how observation depends on measured and missing values.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html
:::

## Method {.role-slide}

The object of interest is

$$
P(R=1\mid Y_{\mathrm{obs}},Y_{\mathrm{mis}}).
$$

## Answer {.role-slide}

Values are [**missing completely at random (MCAR)**](https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html) when observation depends on neither observed nor missing measurements.

$$
P(R=1\mid Y_{\mathrm{obs}},Y_{\mathrm{mis}})=P(R=1)
$$

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html
:::

## Answer {.role-slide}

Values are [**missing at random (MAR)**](https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html) when observation may depend on observed measurements but not additionally on the missing value.

$$
P(R=1\mid Y_{\mathrm{obs}},Y_{\mathrm{mis}})=P(R=1\mid Y_{\mathrm{obs}})
$$

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html
:::

## Answer {.role-slide}

Values are [**missing not at random (MNAR)**](https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html) when observation still depends on the unseen value after observed measurements are considered.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html
:::

## Data {.role-slide}

All three simple sentence trials are observed.

Only one of three complex sentence trials is observed.

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

The pattern is compatible with MAR through observed complexity and with MNAR through unseen reading time.

## Challenge {.role-slide}

A plot cannot distinguish MAR from MNAR because it cannot display the unseen values.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

State a mechanism at the participant, session, or trial level where absence occurs.

## Complete case analysis {.section-slide}

What deletion estimates

## Data {.role-slide}

F3 is absent for the three longest of eight fricative tokens.

A software function silently drops those rows.

## Answer {.role-slide}

[**Complete case analysis**](https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html), also called listwise deletion, retains rows observed on every required variable.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html
:::

## Method {.role-slide}

For required variables $J$,

$$
C_i=\prod_{j\in J}R_{ij}.
$$

## Result #1 {.role-slide}

Mean duration over all eight tokens is 135 milliseconds.

## Result #2 {.role-slide}

Mean duration among the five complete tokens is 120 milliseconds.

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

The complete case mean describes tokens with observed duration and F3.

It does not describe all eight tokens.

## Surprising Fact {.role-slide}

If five required variables are independently observed in ninety percent of rows,

$$
P(C_i=1)=.9^5\approx.59.
$$

## Upshot {.role-slide}

Deletion can lose far more rows than any one column suggests and can change the target population.

## Iterative PCA imputation {.section-slide}

Reconstructing missing cells

## Question {.role-slide}

Can correlated acoustic measurements help reconstruct an absent measurement?

## Answer {.role-slide}

[**Iterative PCA imputation**](https://cran.r-project.org/package=missMDA) repeatedly updates missing cells with a low rank reconstruction while fixing observed cells.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

https://cran.r-project.org/package=missMDA
:::

## Method {.role-slide .compact}

Initialize missing cells. Fit a rank $K$ reconstruction. Replace only missing cells. Restore observed measurements. Repeat until the updates stabilize.

Recall [centering and scaling](../../factorization/centering-and-scaling.html) and [reconstruction](../../factorization/reconstruction.html).

## Data {.role-slide}

$$
\mathbf Y=
\begin{pmatrix}
-1&-1\\
0&?\\
1&1
\end{pmatrix}
$$

## Output {.role-slide}

Column mean initialization fills the missing cell with zero.

The rank one reconstruction returns the same matrix.

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

The component count controls which relations inform the reconstruction.

It must be selected without access to the masked values.

## Important Point #2 {.role-slide}

An imputed cell is a prediction under a low rank assumption. It is not an observed measurement.

## Challenge {.role-slide}

PCA imputation may pull rare vowels, nonlinear relations, or extreme values toward the dominant linear structure.

## Validating imputation {.section-slide}

Masking values that are known

## Question {.role-slide}

How can we evaluate reconstruction when the naturally missing values are unknown?

## Approach {.role-slide}

Hide measured values on purpose, fit without them, and compare their reconstructions with the held aside measurements.

This is the [training and test separation](../../model-criticism-and-prediction/training-and-test-data.html) applied to matrix cells.

## Method {.role-slide}

For masked cells $M$,

$$
\operatorname{MSE}(M)=\frac{1}{|M|}\sum_{(i,j)\in M}
(y_{ij}-\widehat y_{ij}^{(-M)})^2.
$$

## Data {.role-slide}

Mask a measured value of $2.9$.

The column mean from the remaining values is $2.5$.

## Output {.role-slide}

$$
(2.9-2.5)^2=.16
$$

The masked value was unavailable during fitting.

## Challenge {.role-slide}

Uniform masks may test common vowels and central values even when natural failures concern rare vowels or extremes.

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

Estimate centering, scaling, component directions, and tuning choices after masking.

Otherwise information from the masked value leaks into its prediction.

## Important Point #2 {.role-slide}

Retain errors by vowel, speaker group, language, and measurement column before averaging.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

Poor reconstruction falsifies an imputation procedure under the tested mask. Low error does not reveal the naturally missing values.

## Conclusion {.section-slide}

Observed values, missing values, and predictions

## Big Question {.role-slide}

What can an analysis claim when some linguistic measurements were never observed?

## Answer {.role-slide .compact}

1. Encode where measurements are absent.
2. Separate visible patterns from assumptions about the missingness mechanism.
3. State which rows a deletion analysis targets.
4. Preserve the distinction between observed and imputed cells.
5. Validate the complete reconstruction procedure under realistic masks.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

No completion procedure establishes its own assumptions. The report must state what was observed, assumed, reconstructed, and still unknown.
